sources.entry: Build a Spring Boot App with User Authentication

summary.title: Getting Started | Securing a Web Application
summary.one_liner: You learn how to protect a Spring MVC web app with a Spring Security login form backed by an in-memory user, restricting a /hello page to signed-in users.
keywords: how to add login to spring boot app
takeaways: Add spring-boot-starter-security and thymeleaf-extras-springsecurity6 to a Gradle or Maven build.
Configure a SecurityFilterChain so / and /home are public and all other paths require authentication.
Create a custom Thymeleaf login page posting to /login and a logout form posting to /logout.
Define an in-memory UserDetailsService with a BCrypt-encoded user, then run the app and test the login flow.
summary.summary: This Spring Getting Started guide builds a small Spring MVC application with Thymeleaf views for a home page and a greeting page. It then adds Spring Security, showing the Gradle and Maven dependencies and a security configuration that permits only the home paths without authentication. The guide covers a custom login view, a sign-out form, and an in-memory user with BCrypt password encoding, with code in Java and Kotlin. It ends by running the app and verifying the redirect to login and sign-in flow.
